# Stage 2 of 2 — assemble the cards

**Workflow:** [`tarot/tarot-02-assemble.json`](../tarot/tarot-02-assemble.json)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Family | `tarot` |
| Nodes | 10 |

| Paid API calls per run | **free** |

| Writes | `tarot/deck-out` |
| Fed by | [tarot-01-generate](tarot-01-generate.md) |

---

Reads the art stage 1 wrote and turns it into finished cards. **No API calls at all**, so
every run here is free and instant. Iterate on the border and the lettering as long as you like.

## The handoff, received

- **The deck definition** comes from `tarot/deck.json`, written by stage 1. Do not retype the
  deck here — loading the same file is what guarantees the two stages agree about names, order
  and scope. Rename a card in stage 1 and this stage letters the new name without being told.
- **The art** comes from `tarot/derived-art/`. Stage 1 named it `00_the-fool.png`, which the
  Slot Loader matches by slug *and* by index prefix, so it maps back onto the right positions
  either way. Check its report anyway.

## What you can do here for free

`border` off gives full-bleed at the same trim size — the same run, both ways, by toggling one
widget. Add a second **Card Frame** node off the same input to get bordered and unbordered in
one pass.

**Set `font_path`.** Pillow's built-in face is fine for placing the block and not fine for print.

## Coming back later

This stage needs nothing but the two folders. A deck generated months ago re-assembles from
its files with no cascade, no keys and no cost — which is the point of the split.
